posts.post_subject: Green laser-pointers - any good for holography?
posts.content_md: Hihi, An article](http://slashdot.org/article.pl/12/28/1853253&tid=159%22%3Earticle) on Slashdot today is about a](http://64.252.62.40.nyud.net:8090/lasershoppe/index.htm%22%3Ea) guy selling 100mW green lasers. I'm currently reading Practical Holography for the first time & will probably order Shoebox Holography shortly, as Saxby recommends it & I get the impression it's more suitable for n00bs wanting to get their hands dirty for the first time, so I'm not in the market for a $699 flash-light right now. But I'm interested to read about diode-pumped cheapies like these. Are these suitable for holography, at all, and if so has anyone got any experiences with them they'd like to share? A bit of searching turns up this](http://search.ebay.co.uk/_W0QQgotopageZ1QQsassZsavvychap%22%3Ethis) guy who sells green laser pointers modified to run at 45mW. His Buy-It-Now prices of £45 make them appear a bargain, but it turns out that he charges](http://www.wickedlasers.com/products.php?var=ok%22%3Echarges) a premium for those which give a decent wattage. Is $389 a good price for a 45mW laser, or do these not have suitable polarisation or coherence? Thanks in advance for any comments, Stroller.

posts.topic_title: Green laser-pointers - any good for holography?
posts.author: edelbrp
posts.post_subject: Green laser-pointers - any good for holography?
posts.content_md:
Hellohello,

I have one of those 5mW green laser pointers. Very cool! They are very useful for holography: they work great as a sort of instant-on safe light, you can illuminate holograms with them (for short durations), and they work great for presentations. 

To make holograms? Probably not. 

You can only keep it on for less than a minute at a time (or it overheats), and in a dark room it is quite visible from the illumination that the beam is barely stable (lots of erratic fuzziness.. mode hop?). Lastly, it's reported that these at best have a coherence length of a few millimeters, meaning that's the best depth you'll get from any hologram you make with it.

For these reasons it might make sense why similar technology green 100mW lasers with long coherence, like [this](http://cgi.ebay.com/ws/eBayISAPI.dll?ViewItem&category=53141&item=3863589912&rd=1&ssPageName=WDVW), sell for more.

If you do buy one, I would recommend Altasnova. He's very honest about what he is selling, and it's a good price (well, quite a bit less than thinkgeek anyway). [(one of his ebay offerings)](http://cgi.ebay.com/ws/eBayISAPI.dll?ViewItem&category=14954&item=5739989316&rd=1) Not to mention he has a 100% rating with 7000+ transactions.

-Phil
